problem:
The substitution $z=\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ can be used to transform the equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+y\operatorname{ln}⁡y=xy
$$

into an equation of the form ${z}^{′}(x)+P(x)z(x)=Q(x).$ What is the function $P(x)?$
worked_solution:
First, we make the substitution

$$
z=\operatorname{ln}⁡y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get 

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{z}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}.
$$

 

Consequently, the original differential equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{z}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+z{e}^{z}=x{e}^{z}\end{aligned}
$$

We now write the above equation in standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x).
$$

In doing so, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{z}(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+z) & =x{e}^{z} \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+z & =x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=1.$
